atlas_home_region_card.compact: A 1960s songcraft lane where folk lyric weight, electric band sound, and vocal harmony become pop-rock language.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It expands what a pop-rock song can talk about. Protest, poetry, personal reflection, and generational unease can now sit beside hooks and harmonies.
atlas_home_region_card.deep: A 1960s songcraft lane where folk lyric weight, electric band sound, and vocal harmony become pop-rock language. It expands what a pop-rock song can talk about. Protest, poetry, personal reflection, and generational unease can now sit beside hooks and harmonies.

region_scene_page.compact: Folk-rock begins when folk songs and topical writing meet drums, electric guitars, and pop radio.
region_scene_page.standard: Folk-rock begins when folk songs and topical writing meet drums, electric guitars, and pop radio. Bob Dylan's Like a Rolling Stone, Simon & Garfunkel's The Sound of Silence, The Mamas & the Papas' Monday, Monday, and The Youngbloods' Get Together give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Folk-rock begins when folk songs and topical writing meet drums, electric guitars, and pop radio. This lane is more lyric-centered than jangle pop alone and less studio-fantastical than psychedelic pop. Bob Dylan's Like a Rolling Stone, Simon & Garfunkel's The Sound of Silence, The Mamas & the Papas' Monday, Monday, and The Youngbloods' Get Together give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
